Detailed Description

direct access to file-system, no abstraction layer.

may be compiled with support for libmagic (the "file" command). if this support was compiled in but the library is not present at run-time, this backend will fall back on a simple filename-extension (".mp3") to MIME-type ("audio/mp3") mapping instead.

may be compiled with support for libacl (for Access Control Lists -- the file-system you use must support these; if they are optional, a mount- option ("acl") may also be necessary). if this support was compiled in and the library is present at run-time, ACLs and default-ACLs can be viewed and modified in evidence.

may be compiled with support for libattr (for Extended Attributes -- the file-system you use must support these; if they are optional, a mount- option ("user_xattr") may also be necessary). if this support was compiled in and the library is present at run-time, EAs can be viewed in evidence.

may be compiled with support for F_NOTIFY (on Linux >=2.4) and/or libfam (for FAM, the File Alteration Monitor). if F_NOTIFY was compiled in and a suitable kernel is deteced at run-time, F_NOTIFY will be used to learn about changes in the file-system. otherwise, if support for FAM was compiled in and the library is present at run-time and the FAM-daemon speaks with us, FAM will be used. otherwise, this backend will fall back on polling directories as a last resort.

by Azundris
